items.t: i remember the homophobia of the 90s etc but i still think that trans rights are a harder sell bc you can’t really do the ‘love is love, it doesn’t affect you so why not’ thing. it is going to affect other ppl in a way that 'just let people be who they are’ doesn’t cover. like w bans on trans girls participating in competitive female sports- you can’t just stop at the 'why not let them call themselves girls’ you have to convince them that it’s not unfair to cis girls. which is a huge difference actually! i see people trying to do this by going 'all this over a dozen kids!’ but that’s not going to convince anyone who thinks its actually unfair- 'so let’s nip it in the bud before its a real problem’ is a totally natural response to that. (the other two responses ive seen are exaggerating what’s going to happen to cis girls & minimizing the importance of girls’ sports (or just being straight up like men don’t have any physical advantage lets get rid of women’s sports, which, um) & neither of those are helpful either lol. you’re not going to convince anyone whose primarily concerned abt cis girls by going 'they’re going to BE FORCED into INVASIVE GENITAL EXAMS before GYM CLASS’ when they can read the policy and see that its an extra form to fill out for them (as it is here) / their doctor when a doctor’s note is already required for school sports (as i understand it is in washington). you’re also not going to convince anyone by being all 'all this over school sports smh’ if they’re motivated by any principle of fairness or equality for cis girls & women. you have to actually convince them to support trans girls in participating in competitive female athletics on the merits of the issue itself! not that youve been making those arguments ofc im just tired of seeing them lol)
